title: Cost Conductor: intelligent prefill simulator + safe quant guardrails
author: Aisha Patel
description: Background: we routinely recommend batching, prefill and quantization defaults in the Console but lack an offline, reproducible estimator and a safe runtime guardrail for live rollouts. This PR adds: 1) a lightweight unit-econ simulator (cost-conductor/sim) that ingests sample request traces and predicts per-token cost/latency for candidate batch/prefill/quant combos; 2) a runtime "cost conductor" controller that converts simulator recommendations into live proposals and enforces safety guardrails (latency SLO, quality regression thresholds, and deterministic fallback to full-precision); 3) an introspection endpoint and Console integration to preview suggested profiles and canary rollout plans. Motivation: reduce manual tuning cycles, eliminate risky quant+batch blindspots, and make suggestions safer to apply automatically. Changeset highlights: - new simulator library in Go with a small WASM-compatible runner for safe Console previews - runtime controller in Python that hooks into the serving scheduler and rollout manager - safety policy engine that checks unit-econ predictions against historical SLO/quality baselines - a small SQL migration to persist suggested profiles and rollout state - Console UI markdown preview and docs page. Checklist: - [x] unit-econ simulator implemented and unit-tested - [x] runtime controller integrated with rollout service - [x] safety policies implemented and covered by integration tests - [x] Console preview and docs added - [x] e2e shadow canary validated on internal workload. Related: ENG-9843 (Cost automation roadmap), ENG-9972 (Runtime rollout APIs). Notes: the simulator is intentionally conservative about cost savings when traces are short or KV cache hit uncertainty is high; runtime controller exposes a feature flag (cost_conductor.enable) for gradual rollout. See release notes and docs for upgrade guidance.

release_notes: Introduce 'Cost Conductor' — automated recommendation and safe rollout for batching, prefill and quantization profiles. Includes an offline unit-econ simulator for reproducible proposals, runtime guardrails to prevent quality or latency regressions, and Console preview. Ops: enable via feature flag cost_conductor.enable and run the migration 20250214_create_conductor_profiles.sql. Backwards compatible; falls back to previous serving defaults on error.
deployment_plan: Canary (shadow traffic) -> 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on violations. Feature flag gated. Run simulator against representative traces before enabling for a customer.
notes_for_support: If customers see higher tail latency after enabling, roll back via feature flag and check safety_engine logs; ensure simulator trace used representative KV cache patterns. SUP-1432 tracks support runbook.
upgrade_instructions: Apply DB migration, enable cost_conductor.enable=false by default, run simulator against recent traces and import proposed profiles before flipping feature flag per-customer.
security_considerations: Simulator runs on sampled traces only, no sensitive payloads are stored; profile proposals persist model/quantization names but not model weights. Feature flag restricts rollout creation to ops-role only.
post_merge_actions: Monitor cost-conductor.metrics.{suggested_savings,applied_profiles,rollbacks} for first 72h; schedule a follow-up to collect real-world delta and compare to simulator predictions.
